name: Bariah
title: Descendant of David's royal line
summary: Bariah is a person mentioned in 1 Chronicles as a descendant of King David through Shemaiah. He belongs to the royal lineage of Judah and is noted in connection with the genealogies recorded during and after the exile in Babylon. His significance lies primarily in his place in David's family tree.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in David's genealogy
keyEvents.description: Bariah is listed as one of the sons of Shemaiah in the genealogy of David's descendants, recorded in 1 Chronicles.

keyEvents.title: Part of the royal lineage after the exile
keyEvents.description: Bariah's lineage shows that David's royal line was preserved and documented even through the Babylonian exile, which was important for Jewish identity and hope.

keyEvents.title: The sons of Shemaiah are counted
keyEvents.description: It is noted that Shemaiah had six sons, including Bariah, showing that the royal lineage continued to grow even during the exile.

keyEvents.title: Connection to the Shecaniah branch
keyEvents.description: Bariah belongs to that branch of David's descendants which goes through Shecaniah, an important branch of the royal line that was carried forward after the return from Babylon.
